title: Hazel and the Horizon
premise: Lior Halloran, a navigator who has spent twenty years hiding among cargo runs, discovers a manifest for the Meridian's Wake — a ship that never flew — bearing their own name and a second identity they don't remember. The name belongs to a cryosleeping backup of themselves, one of thousands of 'spares' the fleet's ruling Concord stored as legal leverage during the war. As the fleet's truce expires, Lior must ally with the Wake's forgotten crew, a found family of stowaways and deserters, to decide whether to wake the Concord's chosen half of humanity or the dissidents the law erased. In the end, Lior wakes both halves in equal measure and broadcasts the full manifest to every ship, dissolving the Concord's leverage and choosing a shared, uncertain future over a rigged one.
about_author: Marguerite Crane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who now writes science fiction from a coastal town that floods every spring. Their work explores how people build justice when the institutions around them have already been sold.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a routine customs sweep of the freighter Kestrel's Lantern, Lior finds a manifest for the Meridian's Wake, a ship officially destroyed twenty years ago — with Lior's name and an unfamiliar second identity listed among the sleepers. The beat is quiet dread: the past has a paper trail.

chapters.title: Backups in the Hold
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior traces the manifest's routing codes to a decommissioned orbital yard and confirms the Wake still exists, its hold full of cryopods the Concord claims as 'contingent assets.' They almost burn the evidence. The beat is the temptation of invisibility, and its cost.

chapters.title: The Stowaway's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A young stowaway mechanic, Sefa, who has been secretly living in the Kestrel's Lantern's hold, reveals she's been reading Lior's private logs for months and knows about the manifest. Instead of blackmail, she offers help. The beat is wary connection — the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Flashback chapter: the war's end, the truce brokered by the Concord, and the night Lior's crew voted to surrender the Wake's sleepers rather than fight. Lior alone abstained, then ran. The beat is guilt reframed — Lior didn't cause the betrayal, but they didn't stop it.

chapters.title: The Name on the Pod
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Infiltrating the yard, Sefa finds the pod labeled with Lior's alternate identity: 'Liora Halloran, witness, do not wake.' The pods are legal evidence, frozen testimony against the Concord. The beat is horror at discovering a person stored as a filing cabinet.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A Concord magistrate, Iven Sorel, boards the Kestrel's Lantern for inspection and lets Lior know, gently, that he knows what they found — and that cooperation means a quiet life. The beat is the law offering comfort as a leash.

chapters.title: Crew of the Never-Flying
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa brings Lior to a drifting habitat of deserters and stowaways who call themselves the Wake's crew, keeping vigil over records of the sleepers for two decades. The beat is Lior meeting the family that formed around their absence.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Knew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Decrypted pod records show the sleepers include both Concord loyalists and dissidents — the Concord kept them mixed so waking any half indicts everyone. The beat is the realization that the archive was designed as a mutual hostage system.

chapters.title: Sorel's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Iven Sorel's POV. Sorel, himself a former Wake crewman who chose the Concord, argues to Lior that waking only the loyalists is mercy: the dissidents' testimony would reignite war. The beat is a sympathetic antagonist making the safe choice sound like love.

chapters.title: The Vote We Never Finished
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Wake crew demands Lior finish the vote they abandoned twenty years ago: which half wakes when the truce expires in thirty days. Lior proposes a third option — wake everyone, all at once, publicly. The crew calls it naive. The beat is hope colliding with scar tissue.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Someone vents atmosphere in the habitat and destroys the decrypted records; a crew member is killed. Suspicion falls on Sefa's old smuggling debts. The beat is grief and the fragility of trust in a small, hunted family.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior traces the sabotage to a crew elder who has been feeding Sorel information, believing partial waking would save the most lives. Instead of vengeance, Lior offers him the truth: Sorel plans to wake no one and scrap the pods. The beat is justice as persuasion, not punishment.

chapters.title: Running the Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A breakneck run through Concord-patrolled space to reach the Wake before the truce expires, using the Kestrel's Lantern's cargo routes as cover. The elder's knowledge gets them through the checkpoints. The beat is the traitor redeeming himself in the navigator's chair beside Lior.

chapters.title: Boarding the Wake
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Aboard the Meridian's Wake at last, Lior walks corridors they half-remember from a life they can't verify, and stands before their own sleeping body. The beat is uncanny grief — meeting the self they might have been.

chapters.title: Liora's Testimony
chapters.summary: Liora's POV (recorded log). The backup left a message: she volunteered as a witness, knowing Lior would run, and forgives them — but warns that the Concord's real leverage is a falsified manifest that could make the dissidents look like war criminals. The beat is absolution with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Fleet Gathers
chapters.summary: Iven Sorel's POV. As the truce expires, the Concord fleet assembles around the yard, and Sorel is ordered to destroy the pods and blame the deserters. He hesitates for the first time in twenty years. The beat is the antagonist's crisis of loyalty.

chapters.title: Thirty Minutes to Truce
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crew races to wake the pods and broadcast the true manifest fleet-wide; Sefa must manually hold the cryo-bay doors against a Concord boarding team. The beat is terror and competence — the stowaway holding the line.

chapters.title: Which Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax: with power for only half the pods, Lior faces the choice they fled twenty years ago — and instead rigs the system to wake everyone sequentially, buying time by broadcasting the falsified-manifest evidence to every bridge in the fleet. The beat is the choice refused in favor of a harder promise.

chapters.title: The Fleet Decides
chapters.summary: Iven Sorel's POV. Confronted fleet-wide with the falsified manifest, ship crews refuse the destroy order; Sorel stands down and arrests his own commanding magistrate. The beat is justice outside the law, executed by the law's own servants.

chapters.title: Waking, One by One
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The slow, painstaking revival of the sleepers — loyalists and dissidents together, meeting their hostages and their witnesses. Sefa, who has no family of record, is claimed by all of them. The beat is found family made literal and fleet-wide.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Navigator
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior sits with their awakened backup, Liora, and they agree neither will be the original — they will split the Kestrel's Lantern's route and the Wake's crew between them, two lives from one debt. The beat is reconciliation with the self, and a future with room in it.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Epilogue: the renamed fleet departs for open, unclaimed space, the truce replaced by a charter written by sleepers and stowaways. Lior plants a hazel sapling from Earth-stock in the Wake's garden bay and watches the horizon line of the galaxy turn. The beat is earned peace — memory kept, justice shared, family chosen.
